summary: The note is a clipped Wikipedia article on the Detroit waste incinerator, also called the Detroit Resource Recovery Facility and Detroit Renewable Power, a waste-to-energy plant at 5700 Russell Street that operated from 1989 to 2019. It describes the plant's capacity, the neighborhood opposition over odors and health concerns, and its demolition from 2022 to 2023. Navigation and boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: A Detroit waste-to-energy incinerator that operated from 1989 to 2019, drew environmental justice opposition, and was demolished in 2022-2023.
key_facts: The Detroit waste incinerator was also known as the Detroit Resource Recovery Facility and as Detroit Renewable Power.
The plant is located at 5700 Russell Street in Detroit and covered 15 acres.
While operating, the plant processed 5,000 tons of waste on a daily basis.
The plant provided energy to 75,000 nearby homes while operating.
Detroit authorities described the plant as the largest municipal solid waste incinerator in Michigan.
Plans for the incinerator were announced in May 1986.
The plant cost approximately $500 million and opened in 1989.
Initially operated by the City of Detroit, the plant was operated by Detroit Renewable Power until March 27, 2019.
Odors from the facility caused complaints from neighboring residents, who also complained about respiratory issues.
Local residents launched a campaign to close the plant, arguing it burned waste from affluent communities while polluting the air near predominantly Black, poorer neighborhoods.
Local group Breathe Free Detroit organized a petition to close the plant.
Demolition of the plant started in 2022 and was managed by Homrich Wrecking company.
The plant's smokestack was demolished on June 11, 2023.
